tool.name: Molecule signature
tool.command: #if $incl_input_alf=="true" python3 '$__tool_directory__/static/update_alphabet.py' '$alphabet_selector.fields.path' updated_alphabet.npz '$input_text' && molsig enumerate --smiles '$input_text' --alphabet updated_alphabet.npz --output analogues_smiles.tsv #else molsig enumerate --smiles '$input_text' --alphabet '$alphabet_selector.fields.path' --output analogues_smiles.tsv #end if

param.name: incl_input_alf
param.label: Include input molecule in alphabet (recommended for molecular design)

tool.help:
**De Novo Molecular Design by Reverse Engineering Fingerprints**
**❔ How to use ?**
**SMILES** *(Compute the ECFP from molecule)*
-Example: *CCO* or *c1ccccc1*
Ready-to-copy SMILES examples:
- Phenazinol : ``C1=CC=C2C(=C1)N=C3C=CC=C(C3=N2)O`` - Linoleic Acid : ``CCCCC/C=C/C/C=C/C/C=C/C/C=C/CCCCC(=O)O`` - Ursolic Acid : ``C[C@@H]1CC[C@@]2(CC[C@@]3(C(=CC[C@H]4[C@]3(CC[C@@H]5[C@@]4(CC[C@@H](C5(C)C)O)C)C)[C@@H]2[C@H]1C)C)C(=O)O`` - Orlistat : ``CCCCCCCCCCC[C@@H](C[C@H]1[C@@H](C(=O)O1)CCCCCC)OC(=O)C(CC(C)C)NC=O``
⟹ Find out more about SMILES: `Wikipedia - SMILES <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Molecular_Input_Line_Entry_System>`_
**Alphabet**::
-MetaNetX (Biology) – 227,717 fragments from 206,338 molecules -eMolecules (Comerciales) – 570,421 fragments from 5 million molecules -ChEMBL (Drug-like) – 712,244 fragments from 1,907,613 molecules -DrugBank (Drugs) – 40,138 fragments from 9,516 molecules
.. class:: infomark
**How does the method work?**
Extended-Connectivity Fingerprints (**ECFPs**) are widely used molecular vectorizations in cheminformatics. They encode local atomic environments into numerical vectors and are commonly used for **QSAR/QSPR**, similarity search, virtual screening, and machine-learning models that predict molecular activities or properties.
Here, we address the inverse problem. Instead of starting from a molecule to predict properties, we start from a fingerprint and ask whether other molecular structures can produce exactly the same ECFP. Such molecules can be seen as fingerprint analogues and may share similar predicted properties in models relying on this representation.
The algorithm uses an **alphabet** of small molecular environments — chemical **Lego bricks**. It searches for combinations whose summed fingerprint exactly matches the input ECFP, formulated as a system of **linear Diophantine equations**. Once compatible fragment combinations are found, the method reconnects them into chemically valid molecular graphs.
.. class:: warningmark
In our experiments, ~91.3% of cases yield no analogue. ECFP collisions are rare, so requiring identical fingerprints imposes a very strong constraint on the molecular space.
Reference alphabet files (ChEMBL, DrugBank, eMolecules, MetaNetX) must be installed by a Galaxy admin and referenced in tool-data/molsig_alphabets.loc. Files are available at: https://zenodo.org/records/22691018
